lines.en: Apparently, what I meant earlier by “I can do anything I want” is “I can stand around and feel awkward while waiting for one of the room’s two tiny inhabitants to return.”
As you may be able to tell by another contemplative walk home, neither one of them ever showed up. So now, there’s nothing left to do but put an end to this night the only way I know how.
By vigorously masturbating in the blue glow of my computer’s light while wondering what has become of me and where I could be if I’d actually apply myself.
Maybe Wakana is onto something. Maybe I should start writing again.
I mean, it’s not like I haven’t tried.
I wanted to submit something for her stupid contest. Just...none of it felt right.
And it’s highly probable that nothing will ever feel right again because I’m not the same person I was back then.
Or at least I think I’m not.
I’m not really sure.
Looking back at the past is kind of difficult when the universe itself is constantly pulling the wool over your eyes.
My efforts are more focused on the future for now.
It’s easier to see.
And there are things there I’ve yet to experience. Things I want to experience because, like any other creature, I’m entirely and helplessly incomplete.
But maybe there’s someone out there-
Someone unexpected-
Who can help complete me in a way no one else would ever anticipate.
: Well, if it isn’t Uta Ushibori.
: What...what are you doing out here? It’s kind of late, isn’t it?
: I’m on my way back from your room.
: My room? But-
: Okay. Hold on one second, mister. I’m gonna need you to empty out your pockets so I can be sure you’re not going around and stealing more precious Uta-chan mementos to defile while Ami is asleep.
: I promise I did not take any of your underwear this time.
: I’m going to need a more specific promise, Sensei. Just saying you didn’t take any leaves open the possibility that I come home to a very sticky surprise in my panty drawer later.
: I didn’t do anything inappropriate.
: Besides breaking into my room, you mean.
: Is it really “breaking in” if the door was unlocked?
: Hah...no. I guess it’s not.
(She’s wrong. It is.)

: Why go all the way over there, though? If you wanted to see me, you could have just called or something. I’ve already proven that I’m willing to drop my responsibilities for you. So it’s not like I’d say no.
: I’ve found that the element of surprise often triggers more interesting events in the past, but I’ll keep that in mind going forward.
: Better question, though. What are you doing out this late?
: Coming back from the bath house. Me and Io wound up talking for a really long time, so she’s just going to sleep there when she’s done cleaning and I am going to go home and be lonely.
: No. You’re going to hang out with me again.
: What? I am?
: Yes. I’ve decided.
: It’s the park scene all over again. How come you keep deciding my schedule for me lately?
: Because you’re letting me. Why would I stop doing a thing I like when I don’t get anything out of putting an end to it?
: I’m not saying I have a problem with it. We’ve just gone so long doing our back-and-forth act that the sudden switch to your assertive side is giving me butterflies.
: Platonic butterflies? Or butterflies that I’m supposed to ignore so your mind doesn’t start spiraling out of control like it did at the park?
: Rest assured, there will be no Uta spiral tonight. There was enough of that at the bath house and I kinda hoped I’d be able to just put all of my feelings on hold until tomorrow morning.
: Should I just...leave you alone then?
: Honestly? You probably should.
: Then-
: But...
: I feel like I’ll really regret it if I...don’t take you up on your offer tonight...
: Even if that offer was...more of a command than anything else.
: You “feel like you’ll regret it?” Correct me if I’m wrong, but weren’t you trying not to feel anything just a few seconds ago?
: Yeah, and then you had to go and ruin that by showing up when I least expected.
: I swear, you have either the worst or the best timing ever. I can’t figure out which one it is.
: I’m not really sure if I get what-
: You don’t have to be sure of anything, just...
: Just take me somewhere no one will see us...
Of course, a million different things run through my head the moment she says that.
But, as desperate as I am for it to mean what I want it to mean, something about the tone of her voice and its mild tremolo tells me there’s more to it than that.
The thing is, those same qualities tell me that if I do follow through...
If I do take her somewhere we can be alone...in the context that I want...
She’d likely give in.
She might want to give in. And making me grab the reins might just be her forcing me to take the first step so she doesn’t have to.
But it might be a test as well.
It might be a trap.
If I were to take her hand and follow my heart down streets dyed red, I wonder what would cross her mind.
I wonder if, somewhere between the clouds of cigarette smoke in a neon-pink lobby and the incense that attempts to mask it, what her last words would be before we turn the key.
I wonder if she’d close her eyes when we kiss.
If she’d wait for me to touch her first, or if she’d get too caught up in the moment and touch me instead.
I wonder if she’d smile. Playfully bite my lip. Ask me to “mess her up” with her cheeks flushed red and her eyes halfway closed.
But among that garden of pleasant thoughts, there’s one unpleasant one.
It whispers to me that the flowers here are not done blooming yet- and that one wrong step could spell their end.
And so I am left with the choice to immerse myself in their unfinished beauty and risk destroying them...
Or to come back when they’re stronger and brighter.
When they can put up with being trampled for a little while.
It’s hard walking away from something so beautiful...so entrancing. But I dilute the difficulty with the idea that I’m walking toward something else instead.
I’m trading one night for thousands. Millions, maybe.
Because taking her anywhere but here would do nothing but show her I’m exactly what she fears the most.
That I’m one more person who cares more about getting her into bed than waking up beside her.
And you know what? Maybe I am.
But if believing I’m not can ease the ever-growing burden placed on her shoulders all those years ago, fuck it.
I can suffer another night of self-pleasure if it means that Uta can gain a little more confidence in the way she approaches me, because I know she’s getting there.
And I know how hard she’s trying not to.
And I don’t want to give her an excuse to turn back around.
I want her to lead me down streets dyed red. I want her to turn the key. To push me down onto some cheap, vibrating mattress.
: Have you been here before, Sensei?
And none of that will happen if I don’t let her bask in the light a little longer.
: Nope. In fact, I have absolutely no idea where we are. I just followed a sign that said “outlook.”
: Well, we are certainly looking out.
: That we are, Uta. That we are.
: Do you like stuff like this, Sensei? Stargazing and nature and all that.
: Not really, no.
: Yeah, I didn’t think so.
: Do you?
: Mmm...nature is fine. I like being outside. The stars and sky and stuff are kind of boring though.
: It appears that I have failed you.
: Hahah! No, you haven’t failed me. I asked you to take me somewhere we can be alone and that’s exactly what you did. This is nice.
: Plus, just because neither one of us is particularly into stargazing doesn’t mean that we can’t acknowledge that the sky is kinda pretty like this, right?
: Yeah, I guess you’ve got a point there.
: Tch. That was your cue to say, “But it’s not nearly as pretty as you, Uta. The stars aren’t even half as bright as your smile.” Or something like that. Way to go.
: I think we both know that you’d just laugh if I actually said something like that.
: It depends on the mood, I think. There’s not really a better time than this to say corny stuff like that, don’t you think?
: It’s just you and me...in the middle of the night...down a winding path with no one else around...
: This sort of thing would be super romantic if I wasn’t just your rental-girlfriend.
: Ah, yes. The girlfriend I rented for the large sum of zero yen.
: Teacher discount. Valid until I graduate. Just make sure to leave me a good review.
: Seems I’m a repeat customer for basically everything you do, huh?
: Yeah, but that’s not really impressive since I only do two things and one of them is just an inside joke.
: Sorry, I guess that line wasn’t direct or flirty enough to hit your romantic criteria. What I really meant to say is “I’ll follow you to the end of the earth.”
: Where does the earth even end?
: Okay, I guess I’m just not good at this. Which, to be fair, is exactly what both of us expected.
: Heheh...no, that one was fine. I’m just being a brat.
: Yeah, what else is new?
: Soooo....
: Stars. Am I right?
: Stars, indeed. I have no idea what Maya sees in them.
: Ah! No talking about other girls on a secret rendezvous. That’s against the rules.

: Well, how else am I going to continue a conversation on a topic I know nothing about? You had a million options for something else to choose and you went right back to a thing we’re both not interested in.
: There’s gotta be something! Like...
: Like...what’s your favorite constellation?
: Probably...
: The Summer Triangle.
: Ooooh. Romantic.
: It’s the only one I know anything about.
: Altair and Vega, right? I remember that story from some camp thingy I went to when I was little. It’s actually pretty sad when you really think about it, isn’t it?
: The Altair and Vega story? Or the fact that you used to go camping?
: Hey! There’s nothing wrong with camping. Like I said, nature is fine. Besides, it was less of an actual “camping” thing and more of just a way for kids to meet and play with each other and stuff.
: The sky was really nice in Nara, though. It felt...bigger.
: Yeah, well, Nara didn’t have the same level of light pollution we have here. The urban district’s effect probably covers all of Kumon-mi.
: You think so? I think the sky looks pretty clear some nights.
: It doesn’t happen all the time, but...tonight for example. This is beautiful.
: It’s just not Nara.
: You really miss it there, don’t you?
: Sometimes, yeah.
: I like being close to the city. But every once in a while, there’s a night like tonight where I think it’d be nice to be somewhere a little more peaceful.
: It’s harder to relax over here, you know? There’s always something going on. Especially in the dorms since there are friggin’ twenty of us.
: Sometimes, I just miss my old futon. And the way my nightlight lit up the shoji whenever I went to sleep. And the fifteen deer who lived in our living room.
: I feel like that last one is an exaggeration even by Nara standards.
: What would you know? You’ve never been there.
: I’ve never had a reason to go.
: Do you want one?
: I have no interest in meeting your parents, Uta.
: We don’t have to go when they’re around. It can be just you and me.
: Is this about that “Uta-sanctioned tour” or whatever it was you mentioned last time we talked about this?
: Mmm...yes and no.
: There would obviously still be a tour. Just my reasons for inviting you are a little different from wanting to show you more about me now.
: Different how?
: I’d tell you, but I’d have to kill you.
: Then kill me. I want to know.
: Are you sure? If you die, you’ll never get to meet the council of living room deer and trade them a piece of oak bark in exchange for eternal life.
: Nara sure has some strange customs.
: If only Grandpa had some oak bark...
: And here we go again.
: Hmhmhm...ahahah! Hahahah!
: I’m glad that you’re at least getting a laugh at how uncomfortable you make everyone whenever you bring your grandfather up.
: It’s not that! It’s not that...
: I just...
: Uta?
: I’m really stupid, Sensei.
: I know that already.
: You only know half of it and it’s not the half I’m talking about.
: Well, then tell me the half you’re talking about or I’m just going to keep accidentally insulting you.
: Even if you have to kill me afterward. It’s fine.
: Hahah...fuck.
: Fuck fuck fuck fuck fuck.
: I agree. Good talk.
: Sensei, I...
: You...
: Wow. You’re really bad at this.
: Shut up! I want to do this more often! That’s what I wanted to say!
: Is that all you wanted to say?
: No! But just that was hard and it’s all I can say right now!
: Uta-
: No, listen! I...
: You’re...
: Mngh...
: Like I said earlier...me and Io talked about a lot of stuff tonight....And you were one of the things we talked about.
: I still don’t...I don’t fully get what it would be like for all three of us to be a thing and...that’s not something I’m really...uh...
: Anyway, there was...there was something she said to me about how...how she sees the two of us. And how she thinks we’d...um...
: She thinks we’re a good match, doesn’t she?
: Sensei, when I’m with you...it’s like...
: It’s like there’s a third Uta.
: It’s not just Uta and Uta-chan anymore, there’s like...a broken one too. Or a...more broken one, I guess.
: And all she does is wonder what you’re thinking of her and whether or not she’s saying the right stuff or...
: Or just...trying to make you laugh. Or smile...Or like her...and I don’t know how to make it stop.
: Do you want it to stop?
: No. Because having all of those things going crazy inside of my head stops me from thinking about all the stuff I hate about myself.
: But at the same time, I’m worried you’re going to hate me. And Io says you won’t, but-
: Io’s right. I won’t.
: But what if you change your mind?
: My...situation...
: It wasn’t just one picture...and it wasn’t just one guy either. I don’t think I made that...clear last time.
: It was the one guy who took things too far, yeah...but...there were others before him. And they could still have pictures of me that I don’t even know about.
: You don’t have to-
: No, I do have to tell you this because I don’t want you to waste your time on someone who isn’t worth it! And I don’t want to get my hopes up just to have you leave when you realize what I am!
: You’re not what you think you are.
: No, I’m not what you think I am!
: I’m not just some girl who made one stupid decision when she was little and wound up getting screwed over! I made a million of them! And I liked it!
: And...and I’d probably still like it if it never came back and bit me in the ass! Like, who even knows what I’d be doing now if that never happened?!
: But it did happen. And it changed you.

: Except it didn’t change me. The only thing it changed is who I’m in contact with and how reluctant I am to let anyone in. I’m still the same filthy pervert I was back then, I just keep it to myself now.
: So...if I were to have taken you back to a love hotel tonight instead of here, what do you think would have happened?
: I think...
: I think I probably would have made another bad decision...
: Would you have liked that more than this?
: Would you have preferred we did that? Or are you happy we came here instead?
: To be honest, I wanted to take you to a hotel. It was the first thing I thought of.
: Then...why would you...
: To show you that there’s more to you than just that — which is something I’m pretty sure you’re aware of, yet you keep bringing your past to the forefront because, like you said-
: I’m reluctant to let anyone in...
: Bingo.
: I’m really happy we came here instead...
: I knew you would be. That’s why I did it.
: Ugh...damn it, Io. How come you’re always so wrong when it comes to yourself, but you hit all the nails with my name on them right on the head?
: She is a builder after all.
: Does my past really not gross you out, Sensei?
: Did I not...make it clear enough just how young I was when all of this happened?
: I’m not concerned about the past. I’m more focused on spending time with the two- or apparently three Utas I have here right now.
: And if one of those Utas starts to want more from you than you’re able to give...what then?
: I’ll just take something from her to make up for it.
: And if she doesn’t have anything to give?
: Then she’s probably just not looking hard enough.
: Are you regretting your choice to hang out with me tonight yet?
: I would never.
: Are you regretting inviting me?
: Nope. All good here.
: That’s reassuring.
: Do it more often.
: Do what? Invite you out?
: Yeah.
: Spend all of your free time on me from now on.
: Every single second of it.
: Is my money not enough?
: You can keep your money. What I really want is you.
: Can I take that as an official confession?
: Not yet.
: Well, how long am I going to have to wait for one? Because all signs within a ten mile radius point to you having feelings for me.
: Feelings? What are those? I thought I said I was done with them tonight.
: That was like three hours and three hundred feelings ago.
: Three hours? There’s no way it’s been- oh my God, it’s been three hours.
: Do you need to start heading back?
: Am I going to get in trouble for sleeping in class tomorrow?
: Do you ever?
: Good point.
: Another hour wouldn’t hurt...
One hour becomes two.
Then two becomes three.
And before I know it, my walk back home is illuminated by the glow of the rising sun.
I met another match tonight.
I hope I’ll see her again tomorrow.
Uta’s affection has increased to [uta_love]!
